solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pinch a bit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to steal or grab something quickly
second meaning: a simple jointed mouthpiece for a horse's bridle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as 'steal a little', but the two halves are separate meanings: a verb for nicking and a noun from horse tack.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaffle is informal British slang for stealing, and it is also the name of a common type of bridle bit.

clue.text: Like some guns mobster and hood arranged together

indicators.note: arranged signals that the two gangland words are pooled and their letters reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangster and a thug grouped together, alongside their firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: The gangland words sit nicely with guns, which hides that they are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothbore gun has a barrel without rifling grooves, such as a shotgun or musket.

clue.text: Stomach can be awfully bad with old people

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of bad are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
men is a crossword stand-in for people in general

explanation.surface: Elderly people's digestion can turn very upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the belly, the part of the body containing the stomach and gut.

clue.text: With excellent degree, boy may finally become White House occupant

parts.note: a first is the top class of British university degree, the excellent result
a lad is a young man

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it in the clue

parts.note: the word may ends in Y, the letter taken

explanation.surface: A young man with a top-class degree may end up living in the presidential residence.
explanation.walkthrough: A first is the highest grade of British honours degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Lady is the wife of the US President, who lives in the White House.

clue.text: This artist does a lot of eating out

definitions.meaning: the kind of artist who makes prints from plates corroded by acid
the surface suggests dining at restaurants; read cryptically it is acid eating into a metal plate

explanation.definitionFit: An etcher makes prints by letting acid bite away lines in a metal plate, eating it out.

clue.text: One is a fool to take exercise

definitions.note: the phrase describes a person, standing for the noun

parts.note: to do drugs is to take them, so the verb 'do' stands in for take
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A warning that anyone who sets out to work up a sweat must be an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also slang for drugs, which ties in with 'take' read as taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, someone who behaves like an idiot.

clue.text: Give a name to unopened flower that's coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a bud is a flower not yet opened

explanation.surface: Naming a flower bud as it begins to sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to give them a nickname or title.

clue.text: Photo captures an outbreak of terror

indicators.note: captures says the photo word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: pic is short for picture
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news photograph catches the moment fear breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is a sudden spreading wave of fear.

clue.text: Command a fraternity of knights

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an instruction given with authority
second meaning: a society such as the ... of the Garter or the Knights Templar

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like issuing a command to a band of knights; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an authoritative instruction and an organised religious or chivalric brotherhood.

clue.text: Front of lorry with one secure storage unit

parts.note: the cab is the driver's compartment at the front of a lorry (a truck)
to net a fish or a deal is to secure it

explanation.surface: Describes a lorry with a lockable compartment for storing goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front of lorry' looks like an instruction to take the letter L, but here it means the whole driver's cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with shelves or drawers for keeping things in.

clue.text: Time to publish daily: material very thin

parts.note: to issue a book or statement is to publish it
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Time to bring out the daily newspaper, though its content is flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very thin' looks like a criticism of the newspaper's content, but it describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue paper is very fine, almost translucent paper used for wrapping.

clue.text: Cat is almost grave

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a tomb is a burial place

explanation.surface: Suggests a cat with a very solemn, serious demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like an adjective meaning serious, but it is the noun for a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom is the standard name for a male cat, so cat defines it by a broader term.

clue.text: These endless marks of approval for remote parts of country

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the word these is used as written before being cut short
ticks are the check marks a teacher puts beside correct answers

explanation.surface: Someone giving an endless stream of approving marks to far-flung rural regions.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticks is an informal term for rural areas far from towns, the back of beyond.

clue.text: Title of business admen rate poorly

indicators.note: poorly suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advertising men give a company's name a low score.
explanation.walkthrough: Admen are advertising executives, who naturally care about a company's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the name under which a company does business, or a brand name.

clue.text: Snooty type returned top-quality little tree

indicators.note: returned means the word for the snooty type is sent back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: a snob looks down on others
A1 is first-rate; the 1 is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A haughty person brought back a superb miniature tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a dwarf tree grown in a pot, kept small by careful pruning.

clue.text: Come down by gold carriage

parts.note: an aircraft or bird lands when it comes down
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An invitation to descend next to a golden horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Allowed to be put into legal document, or taken out

indicators.note: to be put into says the permission word goes inside the document word

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document, such as one for property
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Something permitted to be inserted in a contract, or else struck from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets 'put into' against 'taken out' as opposites; the first is the insertion signal and the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted text has been removed or struck out of a document.

clue.text: Chap regularly raised beer: is it so tempting for a Persian?

definitions.text: is it so tempting for a Persian?
definitions.note: a Persian is a breed of cat; the question asks after something cats find irresistible

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word for a man

parts.note: taking the first and third letters of chap gives its regular letters

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a pint is a standard glass of beer

explanation.surface: A man lifting his beer wonders whether it would appeal to someone from Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: Persian looks like a person from Persia, but here it is the long-haired cat breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a mint-family plant whose scent excites and attracts cats.

clue.text: Money earned, from such in-stock garments?

definitions.note: plural garments for the answer, which names such clothes

parts.note: the ready is old British slang for cash
to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Takings earned from selling off-the-peg clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' (or 'readies') is informal British slang for money in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made clothes are made in standard sizes and sold off the peg rather than tailored to order.

clue.text: Cancel yearbook, having lost one article

indicators.note: having lost means a piece is dropped from the yearbook word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Scrapping a yearly publication after one item went missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, as a marriage or contract.

clue.text: At last install a power circuit

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: install ends in the letter L, the one picked out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finally fitting an electrical power circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as 'finally', but it picks the last letter of install.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap is one complete circuit of a racetrack.

clue.text: As local inhabitant, study one form of Buddhism

parts.note: a den is a private room for working or relaxing
Zen is the school of Buddhism stressing meditation

explanation.surface: A resident who studies a particular branch of Buddhist practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A denizen is a resident or inhabitant of a particular place.

clue.text: Nothing to fasten garment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for zero, nothing at all
second meaning: to do up clothing with a ... fastener

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as having nothing with which to do up your clothes; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip means zero in informal speech, and as a verb it means to close a zipper on clothing.

clue.text: Behave badly in a court — revolting

parts.note: taken as written
people who are up in arms are in revolt

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaving in a courtroom, in a disgusting way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'disgusting', but here it means rebelling, which is UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or play up, as children or machines do.

clue.text: Go mad, following insolence

parts.note: lip is cheeky backchat

explanation.surface: Someone losing their temper after being cheeked.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is to lose control and become suddenly angry or crazy.

clue.text: Barrister? A senior one faces pressure

definitions.note: the question mark flags that a barrister is one example of the answer

indicators.note: faces says the senior figure stands up against the pressure letter, set right next to it

parts.note: a leader is the senior person in a group, and in court the senior barrister in a case

explanation.surface: Asks whether a senior lawyer is coming under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleader is one who argues a case in court, and a barrister is such an advocate.
